answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can charge superlinear identity fees: the first identity pays a small base fee, but each extra identity funded from the same funding thread costs quadratically more, so running a hundred clones costs far more than a hundred honest agents. A velvet-smooth onboarding for one genuine agent stays cheap, while a river of copycat accounts quickly drains the attacker's budget before it earns anything. Fees taken from clones are burned, not redistributed, so there is no rebate to game.
